leave_behind.text: SEAT-01 reads EVERY entry in `otherWorktrees` as kind "extra" and refuses writes from it, whatever the entry's own `kind` field says -- so 'register the lane' cannot be done by analogy with a neighbouring lane's entry that happens to sit there. The register's working convention for a /tmp factory lane is an entry in the seat's `repos` (path AND worktree both the clone), as 20+ siblings do. And the check is not a reading of the file: import the gate's own `evaluate({worktree})` and observe `allow:true`. My first attempt passed a file review and failed the gate.

A drift control that compares the walk against LDT **main** is not the same control as one that compares it against the DEPLOYED revision, and the difference is not academic here: production has served 9ce30b81 since 2026-09-16T20:28Z while three later deploy runs shipped images without moving traffic (their canary/traffic jobs are SKIPPED). Any control that reads a repo cannot see a revision that lags it. Pair every such control with a runtime channel that records what the surface actually said -- here, `declinedRetirement.byRefusalError`.

`gcloud run revisions list` sorted by creation time is what settles 'what is serving', not a service's latest-ready name or a deploy run's green check: the deploy workflow can build and push an image while every traffic-shifting job is skipped, and the newest revision by creation timestamp can be a day older than the newest successful deploy run.

Do not try to read cloudbuild image provenance for commit attribution: `gcloud artifacts docker images describe <digest> --format=yaml(buildDetails.provenance)` returns null for both cortex-api digests, so a revision's source commit has to be inferred from revision creation timestamps + deploy-run head SHAs. Also: node's `fetch` cannot reach smartsite.cloud from this host (`UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE`; a TLS-intercepting leaf), so live probes must use `curl.exe`; and PowerShell's `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` writes a BOM that breaks `JSON.parse` on the artifact it just wrote -- strip it or write JSON from node.

The two re-walks this close is partial on: Hays run eb1d2676-df0c-4432-afb8-629d5808d6a1 (expected 16/16 RECORD_RETIRED, 0 BP-MEANING-01, walk verdict pass -- half (ii) is already satisfied for all 16 nodes, measured) and Williamson 48491 (unmeasured by this lane). Merge #166 first; do not re-pin _LDT_SHA for this change, since the walk reads the serve, not the bake.

The sweep namespace: 15 of the 52 swept ids in 48209 have no parcel-map row, and 2 of 3 sampled passing ids serve an address that contradicts the account row the sweep keyed on (the serve itself discloses it via situsAddressSupersededClaim). The sweep selects from the account namespace while node ids are map ids; the identity/vintage question this exposes is P-178's, and the measurement is in _inbox/2026-09-17_p301-walk-record-retired_sweep-namespace.json.

The `staging` tag (cortex-api-00765-gip) serves RETIRED nodes as baked 200 cards and answers not_baked for unbaked ones -- a third behaviour, pre-P-206 and pre-P-180-exclusion. Any future walk pointed at that tag will fail those nodes for a reason no walk-side change can fix, and it will look exactly like this lane's original defect. Whoever next grades a walk should record which revision answered.

`declinedRefusalCarriedRetirement` is now recorded on every declined-retirement grade and nothing consumes it yet. It is the alarm for 'the serve started asserting retirements in the body without the store agreeing'; the next reader of a rollback should decide the threshold at which it becomes a finding rather than a field.
